title: Errors and validation boundaries

objectives.text: Validate types, ranges and required fields without silently coercing bad data.
Distinguish reject-whole-input from partial-acceptance policies and catch only expected errors.

blocks.markdown: An external value is not trustworthy just because it arrived in a dictionary. A boundary validates the contract before computing or committing a result. Our quantity contract accepts nonnegative Python integers but excludes bool. Zero is a valid quantity for this lesson calculation; another interface may reject it. Policy differences must be stated rather than inferred from earlier examples.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 621, followed by rejected four times. Exact type(... ) is int is a deliberate boundary excluding bool and integer subclasses.

blocks.markdown: An exception distinguishes invalid input from a legitimate numeric result. Returning zero on failure can hide a rejected record as a valid zero-notional trade. The caller can catch ValueError at a documented boundary, report the reason, or reject the whole batch. Do not catch Exception around everything and label programming bugs or I/O failures as normal invalid-input events.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 6, then batch rejected. No partial total is returned for the invalid batch.

blocks.markdown: This function computes only a local result. A later production pipeline may write external state: then validation and transaction boundaries must ensure an invalid batch does not leave a half-committed result. Merely raising an exception does not undo earlier file writes, network calls or database commits. The code here demonstrates a policy, not a distributed transaction.

int("3") can be a legitimate explicitly declared parsing step. int(3.9) truncates, and accepting True as 1 can be surprising. Parsing, validation and rounding are different operations. Do not sprinkle casts into arithmetic as a substitute for an input contract.

Independent transfer: write validate_trade(record). Require exactly the fields trade_id, price_cents, quantity_shares; trade_id is a nonempty string; the two numeric fields follow the nonnegative exact-int rule above. Return a new dictionary with the validated values and leave the input unchanged. Raise ValueError for missing/extra fields, wrong types or negative amounts. State that this is a synthetic strict schema, not a universal trade format. Test the missing-field and bool cases separately.

Technical references: [Python errors tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html) for raising and handling selected exceptions. The financial schemas, policies and synthetic cases in this lesson are declared teaching contracts, not claims about a particular venue or employer.

summary: Validate explicit contracts before effects. Reject invalid input visibly; zero is not an error marker. Exceptions do not roll back prior external effects, and partial acceptance is a separate stated policy.
